nodes.summary: Let $L_{2,k}$ denote the number of right-truncatable square-free numbers with exactly $k$ digits in base $2$. The real series $E_2 = \sum_{k \ge 1} L_{2,k} / 2^k$ satisfies $636163720502 / 2^{38} \le E_2 \le 636163930777 / 2^{38}$.
nodes.title: Bounds on the binary expected square-free walk length

nodes.summary: For every prime $p_0$ there is a sequence of primes $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ starting at $p_0$ such that for every $i \ge 1$ there are integers $n_i \ge 1$ and $k_i$ with $0 < k_i < 10^{n_i}$ and $p_i = 10^{n_i} p_{i-1} + k_i$; that is, each term is obtained from the previous one by appending $n_i$ decimal digits on the right.
nodes.title: Walking to infinity on primes by appending decimal digits

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the $k$-th term $e_k$ of the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ satisfies $e_k + 1 = 2^k (p + 1)$, that is, $e_k = 2^k (p + 1) - 1$.
nodes.title: Closed form of the extended Cunningham chain

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $e_0 = p, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ be the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$. For every $n \ge 1$ there is $i \ge 1$ such that none of $e_i, e_{i+1}, \ldots, e_{i+n-1}$ is prime.
nodes.title: Extended Cunningham chains generated by primes contain arbitrarily long composite runs

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the terms of the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ satisfy $e_{k+1} = 2 e_k + 1$.
nodes.title: Recurrence of the extended Cunningham chain

nodes.summary: The extended Cunningham chain $e_0, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ generated by $2$ has $e_1 = 5$, $e_2 = 11$ and $e_3 = 23$.
nodes.title: First terms of the extended Cunningham chain generated by 2

nodes.summary: For every natural number $p$, the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ has initial term $e_0 = p$.
nodes.title: Initial term of the extended Cunningham chain

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ is the sequence $e_0, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ of natural numbers given by $e_0 = p$ and $e_k = 2 e_{k-1} + 1$ for $k \ge 1$; in binary, $e_k$ is obtained from $p$ by appending $k$ digits $1$ on the right.
nodes.title: Extended Cunningham chain

nodes.summary: There is no sequence of primes $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ such that for every $i \ge 0$ there are $n \in \{1, 2\}$ and a natural number $k < 2^n$ with $p_{i+1} = 2^n p_i + k$. That is, starting from any prime, one cannot walk to infinity on primes by appending one or two binary digits at a time on the right.
nodes.title: No binary prime walk to infinity in steps of one or two digits

nodes.summary: Let $L_{b,k}$ denote the number of right-truncatable square-free numbers with exactly $k$ digits in base $b$. Then $L_{2,1} = 1$, $L_{2,2} = 2$, $L_{2,3} = 3$, $L_{2,4} = 5$ and $L_{10,1} = 6$.
nodes.title: Small counts of right-truncatable square-free numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $k$, $L_{b,k}$ is the number of right-truncatable square-free numbers with exactly $k$ digits in base $b$: the number of natural numbers $x$ with $b^{k-1} \le x < b^k$ such that $\lfloor x / b^{\ell} \rfloor$ is square-free for every $\ell \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$. When $k = 0$ the range is empty, so $L_{b,0} = 0$.
nodes.title: Counting right-truncatable square-free numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \ge \lceil \log_2 (p + 1) \rceil + 2$. Then $2^k - (p + 1)$ is not a power of $2$: there is no natural number $m$ with $2^k - (p + 1) = 2^m$.
nodes.title: A power of two minus a much smaller positive number is not a power of two

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
